I've always taped my webcam (use a piece of opaque cardboard over the camera aperture too - masking tape is translucent and duct tape leaves much to be desired).

Because cameras can be turned on remotely, but a piece of black electrical tape cannot be removed remotely.
I get that, but they've been doing it since they've had a computer with a camera. That's paranoia if that's your first response.

That's not paranoia, that's just common sense from anyone who understands how networked anything works and what the risks are. You don't extinguish matches by flicking them into your gas tank because that has obvious risks, and you don't leave connected web cams with uncovered lenses sitting around because that has obvious risks too.
What's that saying? Just because you're paranoid doesn't mean they aren't after you?

If you are truly scared because you believe that at any moment anyone could install a malicious app in your computer to control your webcam you should stop using computers at all because there are worse things like keyloggers, and those things cannot be stopped with tape.
Just because there are worse things out there doesn't mean that you cannot take precautions for less bad things.

You should be more concerned about keylogger and Trojans as they contribute to you possibly losing money or you identity.

And if you are properly dealing with those two points then you are also automatically dealing with webcam malware and microphone rappers as the solution is the same.

Patch your system regularly, check the program you are going to install is as intended, run antivirus, use complex passwords and don't re-use passwords.
